author: The hMailServer maintainers, Progressive Robot Ltd
tooling: Written by hand; one statement per advisory dismissed as not affecting the project, as SECURITY.md (Vulnerability management policy) requires. No statements means every advisory raised against a component of this project has been fixed rather than dismissed.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-22184
vulnerability.description: zlib's contrib/untgz (a sample tar extractor shipped in zlib's source tree), found against zlib 1.3.1 by the dependency-scan job's OSV query of 25 September 2026.

statements.impact_statement: hMailServer vendors ten of zlib's C files and their headers (hmailserver/source/Server/zlib: adler32, compress, crc32, deflate, inffast, inflate, inftrees, trees, uncompr, zutil); contrib/ is not vendored, untgz is compiled into nothing, and zlib 1.3.2 removed it upstream.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-27171
vulnerability.description: Unbounded CPU use in zlib's crc32_combine64 (and crc32_combine_gen64) with a negative length, fixed in zlib 1.3.2; found against zlib 1.3.1 by the dependency-scan job's OSV query of 25 September 2026.

statements.impact_statement: No hMailServer source calls crc32_combine, crc32_combine64, crc32_combine_gen64 or crc32_combine_op: the server calls deflateInit, deflateInit2, deflate, deflateBound, deflateEnd, inflateInit, inflateInit2, inflate, inflateEnd and crc32, and nothing else of zlib's. The vendored zlib was moved to 1.3.2, which carries the fix, on 25 September 2026.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-3381
vulnerability.description: An advisory for Perl's Compress::Raw::Zlib module, which bundles zlib, recorded against zlib's repository; found against zlib 1.3.1 by the dependency-scan job's OSV query of 25 September 2026.

statements.impact_statement: The affected component is Perl's Compress::Raw::Zlib, not zlib as hMailServer vendors and compiles it: no Perl module is part of hMailServer, and no Perl runs in it.

vulnerability.name: OSV-2024-112
vulnerability.description: An OSS-Fuzz crash report in Boost.Graph's graphviz reader (read_graphviz), found against Boost 1.92.0 by the dependency-scan job's OSV query of 25 September 2026.

statements.impact_statement: No hMailServer source includes a Boost.Graph header or reads graphviz, and the compiled library the graphviz reader lives in is neither built nor linked: libraries/build-boost.ps1 builds thread, filesystem, regex, chrono and atomic for the Windows build, and the Linux build links thread, chrono and filesystem. None of Boost.Graph's code is in any hMailServer binary.

vulnerability.name: OSV-2024-914
vulnerability.description: An OSS-Fuzz crash report in Boost.Regex's format-string formatter (the code behind regex_replace and match_results::format), found against Boost 1.92.0 by the dependency-scan job's OSV query of 25 September 2026.

statements.impact_statement: hMailServer uses Boost.Regex to match and to search (RegularExpression.cpp among others), and no source calls regex_replace, regex_merge or match_results::format, so the formatter is never instantiated and no call reaches it.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-102268
vulnerability.description: An advisory against PyJWT 2.13.0 (critical), fixed in 2.14.0; found in build/ci/requirements.txt by the dependency-scan job of batch42's pipeline 2896082335, 30 September 2026.

statements.impact_statement: PyJWT 2.13.0 is installed only into the semgrep CI job's own virtual environment, from build/ci/requirements.txt, as a dependency of semgrep 1.178.0 - the newest semgrep, which pins it to pyjwt[crypto]~=2.13.0 - and of mcp. No hMailServer release file contains it, and nothing the server, its tools or its packages run imports it. The job runs `semgrep scan --metrics off --oss-only` with no login and no token, so no JSON Web Token is decoded, verified or signed and no JWKS is fetched: the code these advisories are in is never reached. PyJWT moves to 2.14.0 or later with the first semgrep release that allows it (build/ci/requirements.in).

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-88378
vulnerability.description: QuickJS commit 04be24600 contains a heap out-of-bounds write in JS_ReadFunctionTag(), the reader of a compiled function in QuickJS's bytecode format (critical); published on 24 September 2026 and fixed in no QuickJS release. Not raised by the dependency-scan job, whose OSV query has no QuickJS data (UNKNOWN); listed against the quickjs source package by Debian's security tracker on 30 September 2026, and so read by hand against the release, as SECURITY.md says.

statements.impact_statement: JS_ReadFunctionTag is reached only through JS_ReadObject, which reads a value or a compiled script back from QuickJS's binary serialization. hMailServer never calls it: the Linux server's event scripts (hmailserver/source/Server/Common/Scripting/ScriptBinding.cpp) are compiled from their source text with JS_Eval and run, and no bytecode is written, stored or read anywhere. In release 2026-06-04, as in 2025-04-26, the engine itself calls JS_ReadObject nowhere; its only callers are in quickjs-libc.c - the os.Worker message channel and js_std_eval_binary, with which a program compiled by qjsc loads its bytecode - and quickjs-libc.c, qjs and qjsc are not in the tree (hmailserver/source/Server/quickjs carries the engine, its regular expression and Unicode libraries, cutils and dtoa only). So no script, and nothing a message carries, can reach the reader. QuickJS moves to the first release that fixes it.
